notes: line 1.1: 'Pōkarekare' is to be agitated, rough, choppy (of water); used of the troubled heart as well.
line 1.2: Waiapu is a river on the East Coast of the North Island; kept as a name.

line 1.3-4: 'Whiti atu koe' is literally 'you cross over'; the sense, that the water will be calm when she crosses, is implied by the following 'marino ana'. 'e' at the ends of lines is a vocative or sung ending, not translated.
line 3.2: 'rīngi' is a loanword from English 'ring'; 'reta' (3.1), 'pene' (4.1) and 'pepa' (4.2) are likewise from 'letter', 'pen', 'paper'.
line 3.4: 'raru raru ana' is 'troubled, in difficulty'; whose trouble it is (the singer's or the people's) is not spelt out; 'I am' is added.
line 4.1: 'Whati whati' is breaking repeatedly (or broken to pieces); rendered 'breaks and breaks'.
line 5.3-4: the source breaks the line after 'i' ('wet with / my tears'); the line division is kept.
